# One substitution channel for message bodies and node attributes

A declared message type is materialized as an ordinary node of the instance.
`{{messages.<type>.<field>}}` and `{{nodes.<node-type>.attribute.<field>}}`
resolve against the same attribute store, so a template author has one channel
to learn rather than two.

## The template

```yaml
name: messages-as-nodes-demo
version: "1"
messages:
  - type: ops/note
    body_schema:
      type: object
      properties:
        text: {type: string}
      required: [text]
nodes:
  - type: plain
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: ops/note
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          text: {type: string, default: from-a-node}

  - type: reader
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: ops/note
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
      - node: plain
        type: attribute/text/changed
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          via_messages:
            type: string
            source: "{{messages.ops/note.text}}"
          via_nodes:
            type: string
            source: "{{nodes.plain.attribute.text}}"
```

## Drive it

```bash
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/nodes"

curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"type":"ops/note","payload":{"text":"from-a-message"}}'

curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/events?instance_id=$IID&limit=500"
```

## What the product does

`ops/note` appears in the instance's node listing as an ordinary node type.

`reader` resolves both directives in the same dispatch and settles with:

```json
{"via_messages": "from-a-message", "via_nodes": "from-a-node"}
```

The value the messages-directive read is an `attribute/text/changed` write on
the message type's own node, so both forms read the same store.

## The namespaces stay apart

Registration refuses a reference in either direction:

- `{{messages.ops/undeclared.text}}` — 400, `unknown message type`
- `{{nodes.ops/note.attribute.text}}` — 400, `unknown node`; the nodes namespace
  is declared node types

An uncovered reference of either form draws the same coverage finding,
`substitution_ref_uncovered`, naming the `subscribes` entry to add — for the
messages form, an entry on `ops/note`; for the nodes form, one on `plain`.

One diagnostic vocabulary across both forms, and a mistake caught before the
template can be deployed.

## The one exception

The two namespaces do not converge on the subscription side. An
`attribute/<key>/changed` edge declared on a message type is refused at
registration with `subscription_message_type_unreachable`, because delivery of a
message only ever manifests as `terminal/success`.
